about_text: ESMira is a tool for running longitudinal studies (ESM, AA, EMA, …). Studies can be created over an online interface und participants can either use iOS, Android or a web-browser.
action_invitation: Invitation to questionnaire using a notification
app_installation_instructions: Study information and app installation instructions
chooseUsernameInstructions: Instructions for choosing a username (Web version)
dayOfMonth: Only at a specific day of the month
fitToShowLinearProgression_label: Show linear regression when r2 fit is bigger as
postInstallInstructions: Instructions after joining (only in app; can be left empty)
webInstallInstructions: Additional app installation instructions (Web version, can be left empty)
webQuestionnaireCompletedInstructions: Instructions after completing a questionnaire (Web version)
conditionTypeOr: Or (At least one condition must be met)
confirm_backup: Do you want to back all data from study %s?
confirm_delete_account: Do you really want to delete the user '%s' ?
confirm_delete_data:
Do you want to remove all data from '%s'?
They can not be restored!
confirm_delete_backups:
Do you want to remove all backups from '%s'?
They cannot be restored!
confirm_delete_plugin: Do you really want to remove the plugin '%s' from ESMira?
confirm_delete_study:
Do you really want to delete the study '%s'?

ALL ITS DATA WILL BE DELETED AS WELL!
confirm_distribute_message:
The following message will be sent:

%s
confirm_delete_error: Do you really want to delete the error report '%s'?
confirm_delete_questionnaire: Do you really want to delete the questionnaire '%s'?
confirm_delete_input: Do you really want to delete this entry?
confirm_delete_inputPage: Do you really want to delete the WHOLE section including all its entries?
confirm_leave_page_unsaved_changes: There are still unsaved changes. Do you really want to leave this site?
reset_study_desc: Permanently deletes all participant data (responses, statistics, events) while keeping the study configuration intact. This cannot be undone.
confirm_reset_study:
Do you really want to reset the study '%s'?

ALL PARTICIPANT DATA WILL BE PERMANENTLY DELETED.
The study configuration will be preserved.

This cannot be undone!
desc_schedule_planned: When the smartphone was set to execute the action of a schedule at a specific time.
desc_schedule_removed: When an already defined schedule was removed (is usually followed by a new "schedule_planned" event)
desc_actions_executed: When the actions of a trigger are executed (Only fired on iOS).
desc_invitation: When a notification, that leads to a questionnaire, was created (only fired on Android).
desc_invitation_missed: When an invitation to a questionnaire was missed.
desc_freeze_study: Blocks any further data change (and incoming messages). Clients will try again at a later time.
desc_language_changed: When the language of the study was changed.
desc_message: When a message on screen was created by a Trigger Action.
desc_notification: When a notification was created by a Trigger Action (only fired on Android).
desc_questionnaire: When a questionnaire was filled out.
desc_qrCode: When this QR code is scanned by the ESMira smartphone app (it does not matter which QR code), this study will be opened. Other QR scanner apps will be lead to the selected url.
desc_rejoined: When the study was joined and there are still old statistics for this study saved in the app.
desc_reminder: When a reminder for an invitation was issued.
desc_requested_reward_code: When the participant requested the generation of a reward code (regardless of wheter or not that was successful).
desc_schedule_changed: When the participant changed the schedule of the study.
desc_skip_this_questionnaire: Will only be triggered by events from other questionnaires (from this study).
desc_specific_questionnaire: Will only be triggered by events from a specific questionnaire.
desc_statistic_viewed: When the participant viewed the statistics.
desc_study_message: When a study message (a message that can be sent to participants over the web interface) was displayed.
download_as_csv: Download as CSV (cells that a spreadsheet could run as a formula get a ' in front)
error_accessKey_wrong_format: Access keys need to start with a character and can only contain characters and numbers.
error_bad_password: Your password has to contain at least 12 characters.
error_create_request_failed: Your browser does not seem to support AJAX-calls. Deactivate javascript to view this page without errors.
error_missing_requiredField: Please fill out all required fields.
error_name_wrongFormat: The name needs to contain at least 3 characters and must not contain special characters except for: -_().
error_not_a_valid_metadata_json: Could not find a valid metadata.json file.
error_not_selected_recipient: You need to select a recipient.
error_no_webWorkers: This browser does not support web Workers
error_plugin_not_compatible: Plugin in not compatible with the current version of ESMira
error_short_message: The message needs to consist of at least 2 characters.
error_short_username: The username needs to consist of at least 3 characters.
error_study_not_compatible: This study does not seem to be compatible with the server. Please update the server.
error_study_not_found: The requested study was not found
error_study_was_changed: The study "%s" was changed since it was last loaded. All local changes were overwritten with the newest version from the server.
heading: Heading
hideUntilCompletion: Only visible for participants who have finished the study.
info_charts_loadingTime: Depending on the size of the study data files and the performance of your computer, some statistics may take some time to load.
info_no_password_forget: Be aware that there is no "forgot password" option.
info_publish: This will increase the version number of this study. This will signal to all participating apps, that a new updated version of this study should be downloaded.
info_timeout_notifications: Removes the notification after the set time. If you provide 0, the notification will never be removed.
info_install_plugin_from_url: Provide an url to the metadata.json file of the plugin.
webapp_description: Instructions shown on the launch card
label: Label
max_value_vas_desc: Will default to 100 if lower than 1.
prompt_image_fileSize: "%s" is a very big file. Are you sure that you want it embed into the studyfile? It could increase the download and processing time of the study.
prompt_input_name: Please select a variable name (it has to be unique over all questionnaires):
questionnaire_outdated: Preview is not up to date anymore. Current version will be displayed after saving the study.
only_at_specific_time: Only at a specific time of day
info_event_triggered_end_only: Event-triggered questionnaires open when the event fires, so only an end time can be set.
notification_include_deadline: Show completion deadline in reminder notification
notification_title_info: Optional. Shown as the notification's title in the web app and the Android app; empty uses the questionnaire title. The message below is the notification text.
questionnaires_can_only_be_completed_onc: Questionnaire can only be filled out once
Questionnaire can only be filled out once per day
questionnaire_ask_at_onboarding: Ask during onboarding (participant app): starts by itself while it is open
questionnaires_can_only_be_completed_per: Questionnaire can only be filled out once per notification
random_fixed_true: On - Points in time will only be chosen once at random and will stay the same for the rest of the study.
random_fixed_false: Off - Points in time will be chosen at random every time.
skip_page_after_secs_info: Automatically skips the section after the provided amount of time (items that must be filled out will be ignored). 0 to disable.
studyTut_install_app: Open the app store of your smartphone and navigate to the installation page of ESMira by clicking this link:
studyTut_participate_chooseYesForQR: When you are asked for a QR code select "Yes".
studyTut_participate_chooseNoForQR: When you are asked for a QR code select "No".
studyTut_participate_description_step_1: All you need is the ESMira app with which you can connect to this study.
studyTut_participate_method_manual: Your phone has <u>no camera</u> and is <u>another device</u>.
studyTut_participate_method_notOnPhone: You have opened this page <u>on another device</u>.
studyTut_participate_method_onPhone: You have opened this page <u>on your smartphone</u>.
studyTut_participate_open_this_website: Open this website on your smartphone.
studyTut_participate_scanQr: Scan the following QR code with your smartphone:
studyTut_participate_selectAccessKeyYes: When you are asked for an access key select "Yes" and enter "%s".
studyTut_participate_selectAccessKeyNo: When you are asked for an access key select "No, join a public study".
studyTut_participate_selectServer: When you are asked for the server, select "Enter manually". Then type in "%s".
studyTut_participate_startApp: Start ESMira on your smartphone and follow the instructions.
input_instruction: Instruction (shown on its own line after the explanation)
input_image_alt_desc: Describe what the image shows for participants who cannot see it. Leave empty only if the image is purely decorative.
input_screen_reader_label_desc: Optional. Becomes the name screen readers announce for this question (the visible text can still be read), e.g. to explain a scale: "Rate your pain from 1, no pain, to 10, worst pain".
input_spoken_text_desc: Optional. Adds a "Listen" button that reads this text aloud to the participant.
title: Title
timeDistance_between_completion_of_quest: Time distance between completion of questionnaire
userEditable_desc: Times of day can be changed by user
xAxisIsNumberRange_label: Treat values on x-axis as number range
info_path_to_data_directory: A folder named "esmira_data", which will contain all data, will be created in this path. PHP must have write permission for this location. Furthermore, you need to make sure that this folder can not be accessed from the internet (an according htaccess file is  placed inside the folder). If you are unsure what to enter, leave the preselected value as it is.
info_init_additional_steps: Some additional server configuration is necessary to make ESMira work as expected. You can find more information [in the wiki]:
info_dataFolder_already_exists: A folder named "esmira_data" already exist at this location. Should the existing folder be reused for ESMira (if you choose "No" the existing folder will be renamed)?
cookie_consent_desc:
For each study, ESMira uses cookies to store the following information:
  • The provided username: To not having to ask for the username every time.
  • Acceptance of the informed consent: To not having to accept the informed consent every time.
  • Status information from specific questionnaire items: Some questionnaires show different items every time. In order to be able to do that, they need to save which items were already shown before.
info_update_container_image: This server runs from a container image, so it cannot update itself here. If it was installed with the self-host kit, run ./update.sh on the server, in the folder it was installed in.
info_snapshot_restore_complete:
Snapshot %s has been successfully restored.

The page will now reload
info_web_update_complete:
ESMira was successfully updated.

The page will now reload and hopefully ESMira will then be super modern an cutting edge! ;)
info_study_is_public: Study is publicly visible. Add one or more access keys to restrict access to it.
info_randomGroups: Each participant will be randomly assigned to a group. This can be used to hide questionnaires for specific groups.
info_languages: Participants will either get the version of this study depending on the language code of their browser / smartphone or, of there is no version for their language, the default version of the study. You have to use valid language codes or the language version will not be detected.
confirm_prerelease_update: The unstable version of ESMira has not been fully tested and might contain breaking bugs. Are you sure you want to continue?
desc_reward_system: If the reward system is enabled, the app gives participants the option to generate a randomized reward code which they are then asked to send to the researcher (to not break anonymity it is important that this code is sent using a channel outside of ESMira because participants usually also need to provide banking details or a home address).
info_reward_email_content: Must contain [[CODE]] which will be replaced by the actual reward code.
calendar_description: Check-in windows day by day, from the same schedule that opens check-ins and sends notifications on every channel. Plan shows a sample participant for the schedule as you edit it; Participants shows each participant's windows and what they completed.
calendar_plan_info: Sample answers to the questions the schedule reads. Wake-up and wearable events come at their fallback, as for a participant without a wearable; random prompts are drawn for this sample participant (each participant gets their own draw in the same range). Times are the participant's local time.
calendar_plan_info_defaults: The schedule reads no answers: wake-up is %s and bedtime %s (the schedule's defaults) unless a wearable or the wake-up check-in reports otherwise. Random prompts are drawn for a sample participant. Times are the participant's local time.
calendar_no_windows: No check-in windows in these days.
calendar_push_info: Each bell is a notification the schedule planned (the prompt and its reminders), with what was logged for it: sent by the server, delivered to the phone, opened by the participant. The log does not name the notification, so events are matched to the planned times by time. "No push logged" can also mean the participant is reached another way (Telegram) or has notifications off.
calendar_overall: %d participants · %s of expected check-ins completed (%d of %d)
calendar_monitor_info: Expected check-ins: each window of a check-in answerable once per window that has closed, and each study day of a check-in answerable once per day. Check-ins answerable any number of times or once in the study are shown but not counted. Completions are the questionnaires the participant uploaded. Select a participant to see their calendar.
calendar_tz_unknown_info: This participant's time zone is not known yet (it is saved with their next answers), so their calendar is shown in UTC.
download_source_for_publication: Consider adding the study source code to your publication so others can replicate your study
info_low_disk_space: ESMira has less only %d Mb disk space left!
hint_to_best_practices: Before you start your study, we recommend taking a look at the best practices in our wiki
confirm_delete_access_key:
Do you really want to delete the access key '%s'?

Unless all access keys are deleted (i.e., study is made public), active participants using this access key will loose access to the study!
input_location_resolution_desc: Resolution from 0 to 15. Use resolution 9 for a good tradeoff between participant anonymity and precision.
image_input_quality_desc: Value from 0 (smallest file size) to 100 (best quality).
confirm_delete_merlin_log: Do you really want to delete the script log '%s'?
likert_vertical_explanation: Use of a vertical Likert scale can prevent display problems when the number of steps is high (more than ~7).
text_script_explanation: If present, the result of this script will replace the shown text of this item.
show_in_disabled_list_desc: Is shown in disabled questionnaires list when not active
prompt_bookmark_name: Please select a name for the bookmark:
snapshot_description: Snapshots are a complete backup of ESMira server files and all its data. When restoring a snapshot, all current data will be deleted and replaced with the data from the snapshot. This can be used to restore the ESMira server to a previous state.
restore_snapshot_confirm:
Are you sure you want to restore this snapshot?

All current data will be lost and cannot be recovered!
show_skip_toast: Display a message when pages are skipped
info_fallback_setup_token: Below you find your new token to setup the fallback system, as well as the URL of this server. In the next step you will need to enter both in the admin panel on the other server.
confirm_delete_inbound_fallback_token: Do you really want to delete the fallback token for '%s'?
fallback_url_parameter_error: Could not get url for fallback token
fallback_ping_success: Connection to %s successful! Remote server replied and accepted the fallback token.
inbound_fallback_token_info: This is the list of all other servers that can use this server as a fallback for studies.
outbound_fallback_token_info: This is the list of all other servers that this server can use as fallback for studies.
study_fallback_info: Using the fallback system will also store this study on another server, so that participants using the QR code can still join the study even if this server is down.
study_over_message: This study is no longer active.
post_study_note: Post-study note (displayed on info pages after study is over)
validator_warning_package_id: Likely not a valid package id
validator_warning_input_binary: Only '0' (for left option) or '1' (for right option) allowed
validator_warning_input_duration: Requires the total number of minutes
signal_time_across_midnight: End of interval is before start. This will result in an interval including midnight and lasting into the next day.
signal_time_faulty: %d time points separated by at least %d minutes cannot be safely scheduled in the specified time frame.
duplicate_access_key: Access key not unique on server
duplicate_access_key_tooltip: This access key is also used by other studies on this server.
add_all_permissions: Add all permissions for a study
hint_study_unpublished: The study is not reachable. Use this during the development phase.
hint_study_published: The study is live. The info page is available online and participants can join the study.
hint_study_over: The study is over. The info page is available online but instructions for joining the study are removed. New participants can no longer join the study.
warning_all_platforms_disabled: Enable at least one platform in the study settings for the study to be available.
publish_info_text_based: If you recruit text-based (e.g., Email, social media) include the link to your info page. The respective QR codes are also available on that page.
publish_info_fallback_link: Additionally you can include the link to the info page on your fallback server, and instruct participants to use it if the first link does not work.
publish_info_flyer_based: If you want to recruit via flyers, posters, etc., use the QR code.
publish_info_difference_links: Use the link to the study information page for participants in the web version of the study. Use the link to the app installation instructions for participants using their smartphones.
publish_info_explanation_qr: If someone scans the QR code without having ESMira installed on their smartphone, their smartphone will open the info page in their browser. If they already have ESMira installed, the smartphone will instead open ESMira and directly forward them into the enrollment process for the study.
urls_instruction_questionnaires: I want to use the Web-versions of the questionnaires (not recommended)
ios_too_many_scheduled_alarms: Your study has a total of %d scheduled notifications (including reminders). Due to system limitations, the maximum the iOS app can handle is %d scheduled notifications. Going beyond this limit can cause problems like participants using iOS only receiving some notifications, or no notifications at all.
warning_questionnaires_not_scheduled: Participants cannot answer these yet, because no check-in opens them (Edit study → Schedule): %s
participant_link_info: Send this link to your participants. It opens the study in their phone's browser, where they can sign up straight away and add the app to their home screen.
desc_qrCode_web: This QR code opens the selected link.
desc_urls_target_study_list: Have the url lead to a study list and not directly to this study (only if more than one study is using the same access key)
access_key_has_no_duplications: This is the only study that uses the access key "%s". When only one study for an access key exists, the urls will still lead directly to this study.
additional_days_active_info: The amount of additional days the study should remain active after no more questionnaires are active.
schedule_start_day_one: Wait until first full study day (the day after joining the study)
schedule_info_start_same_day: This schedule will start on the same day the study is joined.
schedule_info_start_day_one: This schedule will start on the day after the day the study was joined.
schedule_info_start_day_x: Counting the day the study was joined as day 0, this schedule will start on day %d.
use_legacy_scheduling_info: Use an older scheduling logic to determine day offsets. This logic is not dependent full days, but on 24-hour periods since the study was joined (dependent on time of day).
enable_tutorial_mode_info: On their first visit, web participants see an overview of the study's questionnaires and can take a no-submit practice run before starting.
tutorial_offer_prompt: Tutorial offer prompt (the yes/no question after consent)
tutorial_intro_text: Tutorial introduction (shown when the tour begins)
tutorial_practice_questionnaires: Questionnaires offered as a practice run (untick e.g. a check-in identical to another one)
web_only_mode_info: When enabled, iOS/Android-only controls are greyed out across the admin. Use this when participants only take part via the web PWA.
web_only_disabled_note: Not used on this server (web-only mode)
enable_personal_charts_info: When enabled, participants can view their own personal charts (trends, mood, sleep, etc.). Disable to hide the charts section entirely.
charts_visible_only_after_study: Show charts only after study completion
charts_visible_only_after_study_info: When enabled, participants cannot see their charts until the study is marked as over. Useful when early feedback could bias ongoing responses.
enable_web_push_info: After consenting, web participants are asked to allow notifications. The server then sends questionnaire reminders (using each questionnaire's schedule and notification message) even when the app is closed. Requires a VAPID key configured on the server.
web_phone_only: Only allow participation on a smartphone (web)
web_phone_only_info: On computers and tablets the web app does not start the study. It shows an invite page with a QR code to continue on a phone instead. This is a convenience check in the participant's browser, not a security measure. Needs Web ticked under study availability.
web_language_auto: Automatic (study language, then the participant's browser)
web_language_info: The language of the participant web app's buttons and messages. The questions are shown in the study's own language. Parts that are not translated yet appear in English.
message_pacing_wpm_info: When the app or the Telegram bot sends several messages in a row, each waits behind a typing indicator until the previous one has had time to be read at this speed (between 1.2 and 10 seconds per message). 238 is an average adult reading speed; lower values give more time, 0 shows messages at once.
day_start_time_info: A study day runs from this time to the same time the next day: check-ins open "until the day ends" stay open until then, and "once per day" counts per such day (e.g. 04:00, so an evening diary can be finished after midnight). Must be before noon.
participant_permissions_info: What the web app asks participants to allow, based on this study's items. During onboarding, after consent, the app explains why each permission is needed and only then shows the browser's own prompt.
permission_notifications_toggle: Send questionnaire prompts as push notifications (same switch as Edit study → Push notifications)
permission_notifications_not_needed: Not needed by any item: no questionnaire has a schedule.
permission_notifications_off_warning: Scheduled prompts will not reach web participants while this is off.
permission_notifications_nudge_toggle: Ask participants once a day to turn notifications on while their phone or browser does not allow them (web and Android app)
permission_microphone_toggle: Ask for the microphone during onboarding
permission_microphone_not_needed: Not needed by any item: the study has no voice recording.
permission_microphone_first_use: Off: the browser asks the first time a participant records, without an explanation from the app.
web_push_sender_stale: Reminder sender hasn't run in %s — the cron may be down
web_push_sender_never: Reminder sender has never run — check the cron
enable_android_notifications: Enable notifications in the Android app
enable_android_notifications_info: The Android app plans questionnaire notifications on the phone (and fetches wearable prompts from the server). Same content, look, timing and stacking as web push. Unticking stops them for every participant of this study once their app next opens or polls.
study_end_notification: Send a "study complete" message at the end (web push)
study_end_notification_info: When a participant's last check-in has closed or been completed, one silent notification under the study title takes the place of the last reminder on their phone, so a reminder for a check-in that can no longer be done is not left there.
default_study_end_notification: The study has finished. Thank you for taking part!
welcome_notification_missed_info: Participants told the app the welcome notification did not arrive: their reminders may not reach them. They are marked in the table below.
notifications_off_count: %d participants have switched notifications off in the app (they stay in the study).
notification_channel_android_info: Android app: notifications handed to the phone's alarm service and wearable prompts fetched from the server count as sent; arrived = shown on the phone (reported the next time the app is opened).
notification_preview_info: The first days after a participant enrols, as computed by the code that sends them. Title, text, icon and time are identical in the web app and the Android app. Edit the text in each questionnaire's trigger (notification message); random times are drawn per participant within their window; wearable prompts are not shown.
notification_preview_none: No scheduled notifications in the first days after enrolment.
withdraw_participant_confirm:
Withdraw participant %s from the study?

They will receive no further reminders (web push, Android app, chat channels), their push subscription is deleted, and the app resets itself the next time they open it. Re-enrolling with the same participant id lifts this again.
withdraw_participant_info: Stops every reminder for a participant who has left the study or uninstalled the app without signing out. Signing out in the app does this automatically; use this for participants who asked the research team to stop.
erase_participant_info: For a participant who asked the research team to delete their data. Removes their answers (in every copy of the data files), uploaded media, messages, push and chat state, wearable data and all database rows for this study. It cannot be undone. Not covered: combined statistics, backups of the whole server folder, and server error reports.
erase_participant_also_withdraw: Also withdraw the participant (no more reminders; their app resets)
erase_participant_confirm:
Permanently delete ALL data of participant %s in this study?

This removes their answers, media, messages, push and chat state, wearable data and database rows. It cannot be undone.
erase_participant_mismatch: The two participant ids are different
erase_participant_partial: Not everything could be deleted (failed: %s). Run it again, and check the server error reports.
enable_wearables_info: Lets web participants connect a wearable (Withings or Google Health, which also carries Fitbit and Pixel Watch data) from the app. The server then periodically collects their health data. Requires the provider's OAuth credentials configured on the server (cli/wearables_setup.php).
phone_sensing_info: Collects context from the participant's phone. Only the iEMAbot Android app can do this; web and iOS participants are not affected. Participants are asked for any Android permission a sensor needs when they enter the study, and can grant it later from the app's Phone sensing tile. Mention what you collect in the informed consent.
phone_sensing_light_info: Measures the light level (lux) when a questionnaire is opened and when it is submitted. Needs no permission. Stored in prompts.csv.
phone_sensing_activity_info: Records continuously when the participant starts or stops being still, walking, running, cycling or in a vehicle (activity.csv), so the activity before, during and after every prompt is known; the current activity is also added to prompts.csv. Battery-friendly. Needs the Physical activity permission and Google Play services.
phone_sensing_accelerometer_info: Records the raw accelerometer (x, y, z in m/s², including gravity) from a few minutes before each scheduled prompt until a few minutes after it, and while a questionnaire is open (accelerometer.csv). Android shows a notification while recording. Prompts the phone cannot know in advance (e.g. sensor-triggered) are recorded from the moment the questionnaire is opened. Uses much more battery, mobile data and server storage than activity recognition; see the estimate below once it is switched on.
phone_sensing_estimate_info: Raw accelerometer data grows quickly, even though the server stores it compressed (about %d bytes per sample). Adjust the numbers below to your study; they are only used for this estimate. Recording also costs participants battery and mobile data.
phone_sensing_estimate_per_prompt: Per prompt: %s samples, about %s on the server.
phone_sensing_estimate_per_day: Per participant and day: about %s on the server and %s of mobile data for the upload.
phone_sensing_estimate_total: Whole study: %s samples, about %s on the server.
phone_sensing_estimate_large: That is a lot of data. Make sure the server has the disk space, or record fewer minutes around each prompt, fewer samples per second, or use activity recognition instead.
phone_sensing_usage_info: Reads which apps were used, by package name, from Android's usage statistics, from the moment the participant joins. Needs the participant to switch on Usage access for iEMAbot in Android's settings. Daily summaries: foreground time and launches per app and day (usage_daily.csv) plus screen-on time, screen-ons and unlocks per day (screen_daily.csv). Raw events: every time an app comes to the foreground or leaves it, the screen turns on or off and the phone is unlocked (usage_events.csv).
phone_sensing_upload_info: When the app sends what it sensed to the server. Raw accelerometer data and app usage events can use a lot of mobile data; waiting for Wi-Fi spares the participant's data plan but data arrives later. Questionnaire answers are always sent over any connection.
phone_sensing_upload_wifi_preferred: Wi-Fi, or mobile data after waiting
phone_sensing_upload_wifi_only_warning: Participants who are rarely on Wi-Fi may send no sensing data at all.
phone_sensing_participant_network_info: Participants can switch in the app between waiting for Wi-Fi (with the hours above) and sending over any connection. Not offered with Wi-Fi only.
phone_sensing_no_data: No phone sensing data received yet.
wearables_redirect_uri_info: Register this exact URL as the redirect/callback URI in each enabled provider's developer console, or participants' connections will be rejected.
wearables_participants_summary: %d of %d participants have connected a wearable.
wearables_last_event_info: Every notification a provider sends for a participant is kept for the study, whether or not a trigger uses it, until the participant disconnects.
wearables_webhook_not_ready: sensor triggers unavailable: the server cannot receive this provider's notifications yet (see the wearables setup docs)
wearables_participant_needs_reconnect: link no longer valid, participant must reconnect
sensor_event_bed_out: Out of bed (Withings Sleep Analyzer only)
sensor_event_sleep_sensor_ready: Sleep sensor ready after set-up (Withings Sleep Analyzer only)
sensor_event_bed_occupied: Bed occupied, 10-minute status (Withings Sleep Analyzer with Live Sync)
sensor_event_bed_empty: Bed empty, 10-minute status (Withings Sleep Analyzer with Live Sync)
sensor_event_bed_occupied_or_empty: Bed occupied or empty, 10-minute status (Withings Sleep Analyzer with Live Sync)
sensor_window_only: Only react to sensor events within a daily time window
sensor_event_unsupported: The selected provider does not send webhooks for this data type; this trigger will never fire (only the fallback can).
sensor_wearables_disabled: Wearables are not enabled for this study. Enable them in the Wearables section, otherwise participants cannot connect a device.
sensor_provider_not_offered: The selected provider is not among the study's offered wearable providers.
sensor_fallback_enable: If no matching sensor event arrived by a certain time, send the prompt anyway
sensor_fallback_default: If the variable is not set, send at
sensor_fallback_variable_missing: Enter the name of a time item (e.g. habitual_wake_time). Without it, only the fixed time is used.
sensor_fallback_variable_unknown: No time item called "%s" exists in this study. The fallback uses each participant's latest answer to that item, so add one (e.g. in an intake questionnaire).
sensor_fallback_variable_info: Uses each participant's latest answer to that time item (e.g. their habitual wake-up time) plus the offset, so the prompt follows their own routine. Not sent if the prompt was already triggered that day.
sensor_fallback_info: Also covers participants who have not linked a device or whose device did not sync. Not sent if the prompt was already triggered that day.
sensor_fitbit_removed: Fitbit is no longer a supported provider (its legacy Web API is turned off on 30 October 2026). This trigger never fires; choose Google Health, which also carries Fitbit data.
sensor_googlehealth_note: Google Health is the successor of the Fitbit Web API. It needs a Google Cloud project with the Google Health API enabled (unverified projects are capped at 100 users) and a webhook subscriber registered once on this server (cli/wearables_setup.php googlehealth-webhook). Not yet verified against a live account.
telegram_setup_info: Participants can take part in studies through a Telegram bot. In Telegram, message @BotFather, send /newbot and follow the steps. Then paste the token BotFather gives you here. Polling works behind firewalls; a webhook needs this server to be reachable from the internet over https.
telegram_bot_token_replace: New bot token (replaces the current bot)
confirm_telegram_remove_bot: Remove the bot token from this server? Connected participants stay connected and continue once a token is set again.
telegram_stale: has not run for %s, check the cron job
telegram_no_encryption_key: No channel encryption key yet (it is created with the first token)
channels_public_base_url_info: The address of this ESMira server as seen from the internet, e.g. https://iemabot.surrey.ac.uk/esmira/. Used for the webhook and for mini app links.
telegram_availability_info: Also offer the study through the server's Telegram bot. Set it up under Edit study → Telegram.
telegram_not_set_up_on_server: No Telegram bot is set up on this server yet (Server settings → Messaging channels).
enable_telegram_info: Participants join by opening an invite link in Telegram and answer the questionnaires in the chat. Reminders arrive as Telegram messages. Changes take effect once the study is saved.
telegram_allow_handoff: Open slider/keystroke/cognitive items in a Telegram mini app
telegram_allow_handoff_info: When off, sliders are shown as buttons from 0 to 100 in steps of 10, keystroke items become plain typed text and cognitive tasks are skipped.
telegram_invite_unsaved_key: This access key is not saved yet. Save the study before sharing the link.
telegram_participant_invite_info: Whoever opens this link joins as the given participant ID.
telegram_compatibility_summary: %d of %d items are asked directly in the chat.
telegram_compatibility_all_native: All items are asked directly in the chat.
telegram_va_scale_buttons: Shown as buttons from 0 to 100 in steps of 10
telegram_keystrokes_text: Answered as plain typed text, without keystroke timing
telegram_cognitive_skipped: Cognitive task: skipped without the mini app
telegram_relevance_ignored: Condition ignored, the item always shows (only "name == value", "!=" or ">=" is supported)
telegram_page_relevance_ignored: Page condition ignored in Telegram, the page always shows
daily_plan_info: An ordered list of check-ins per day, each with its own time range. A check-in can be answered from its prompt for its response window, or throughout its range; it is prompted at most once, at the start of its range, at a random time inside it, when the participant gets up, or not at all. Windows never overlap, so participants have at most one check-in open at a time and complete each one once a day. By default a check-in never opens before the previous one's window has closed, and an optional cool-down keeps the next check-in closed for a while after one is completed. Works the same in the web app, the Android app and Telegram.
daily_plan_push_off: Web push notifications are off for this study (Push notifications): web participants are not prompted, but the check-ins still open and close on time.
daily_plan_checkins_info: Each end of a range is a clock time, wake-up, the usual wake-up or going to bed plus an offset, or a split point of the waking day (wake-up to the planned bedtime divided into equal parts; point 0 is wake-up, the last point is bedtime). A clock time or wake-up can be on the next day, e.g. until 02:00 after midnight, or until the participant gets out of bed the next morning. Mix them for hybrid ranges, e.g. from wake-up until 11:00, or 19:00 until going to bed. "Split the waking day" gives every check-in an equal part, prompted when it starts; "Fixed windows" gives equal clock-time windows between the fixed wake-up and bedtime, prompted at random. A window that runs into the next day closes when that day's first check-in opens. The usual wake-up is the participant's habitual time (tier 1 under Wake-up) or the fixed time, never the observed one, so a range around it is known before the participant gets up: from -120 to +120 minutes is 06:00-10:00 with the default 08:00. With a cool-down, a check-in opens (and is prompted) no earlier than that many minutes after the participant completed another one; a check-in whose window ends during the cool-down is missed.
daily_plan_segments: Split the waking day into (0 = one part per check-in)
confirm_replace_always_open_checkin:
This questionnaire is open at any time, as often as participants like. Replace that with the check-in you are adding?

Choose Cancel to keep it open at any time as well.
daily_plan_no_checkins: No check-ins yet: no questionnaire is open or prompted.
daily_plan_boundary_split: Split point of the waking day
daily_plan_prompt_random: At a random time in the range
daily_plan_prompt_wake_info: Prompted at the wearable's wake-up event (see Wake-up below). Without one by the usual wake-up plus this grace period, prompted then. Not prompted once answered, and always inside the range.
daily_plan_prompt_wake_no_sensor: Wake-up is not observed from a wearable (see Wake-up below), so this check-in is prompted at the usual wake-up plus the grace period, unless answered by then.
daily_plan_available_prompt: From the prompt, for the response window
daily_plan_cooldown: Cool-down after a completed check-in (0 = off)
daily_plan_own_response_window: Own response window (e.g. a longer one for the evening)
daily_plan_no_questionnaire: Choose the questionnaire for this check-in.
daily_plan_own_triggers_ignored: This questionnaire's own schedule and sensor trigger are ignored while it is in the plan; the plan prompts it. Its notification text and reminders are still used.
daily_plan_segment_out_of_range: A split point is beyond %d, the number of parts the day is split into.
daily_plan_wake_sensor: Observed: wearable event (e.g. Withings "out of bed")
daily_plan_wake_from_checkin: When the participant answers the first check-in
daily_plan_wake_from_checkin_info: The check-in that starts at wake-up can be answered from the start of the wake-up window, before any prompt. Answering it marks wake-up and the rest of the day is recalculated from it, also offline in the web and Android app, so the remaining check-ins spread evenly over the participant's actual day.
daily_plan_no_wake_slot: No check-in starts at wake-up (split point 0, or wake-up + 0 minutes), so no answer can mark wake-up.
daily_plan_wake_info: Wake-up is the earliest observation in the window. If there is none by the fallback time, it is the fallback: tier 1, the participant's latest answer to the time item (e.g. habitual wake-up time from an intake questionnaire) plus the offset, on Saturdays and Sundays their answer to the weekend item if one is set and answered (e.g. habitual wake-up time at weekends); tier 2, the fixed time while they have not answered. With an observation source, the fallback is the latest the day starts: set the offset so participants have time to get up first.
daily_plan_bedtime_info: Going to bed is the first in-bed event of the night inside the window if it comes before the fallback, else the fallback: tier 1, the participant's latest answer to the time item (e.g. habitual bedtime) plus the offset, on Friday and Saturday nights (the nights before a weekend day) their answer to the weekend item if one is set and answered (e.g. habitual bedtime at weekends); tier 2, the fixed time. Split points always use the fallback (the planned bedtime), since the day is divided before the participant goes to bed. A time earlier than wake-up is taken as after midnight. An in-bed event only reaches the server, so the app uses it once it is online.
daily_plan_preview_hint: After saving, the notification preview under Push notifications shows the first days for a participant with the default wake-up and bedtime.
daily_plan_overlap_defer: Prompt the next one when the previous window closes
daily_plan_overlap_truncate: Close the previous window when the next one is prompted
daily_plan_tier1_fallback: If nothing is observed in time, tier 1: participant's habitual time
schedule_info: The study's one schedule: which questionnaires can be answered when, and when participants are prompted, in the web app, the Android app and Telegram. A questionnaire without a check-in is never open.
schedule_unknown_questionnaire: This questionnaire no longer exists. Choose another one or delete the check-in.
schedule_parallel_info: Not part of one check-in at a time: it neither waits for nor shortens other check-ins, and takes no part in the cool-down (e.g. a questionnaire open any time).
schedule_days_info: Days are counted from the day the participant enrolled (day 0). Unticked weekdays are skipped; the dates are optional.
schedule_prompt_event: When a wearable reports an event
schedule_event_fallback_variable: prompt at the participant's answer + offset
schedule_event_fallback_default: At the fixed time while they have not answered
schedule_event_info: Prompted at the first matching event of the day (after the delay), or at the fallback if no event came before it. Until then it is not open, unless it can be answered throughout its range. Events reach only the server, so the app learns them when it is online.
schedule_available_day: from the prompt until the day ends
schedule_limit_none: as often as the participant likes
schedule_auto_start_info: The participant app starts this questionnaire as soon as the participant reaches the study while it is open, before other check-ins (e.g. usual sleep times on day zero).
schedule_text_placeholder: You have a questionnaire to complete.
daily_plan_next_day_time_info: The clock time on the following day, e.g. until 02:00 after midnight or until 10:00 the next morning
daily_plan_next_day_wake_info: The participant's wake-up on the following day (with its fallbacks), e.g. an evening check-in open until they get out of bed
